title: Simulations of Texture Evolution in the Near-Surface Region During Aluminum Rolling
version: Cantergiani et al.; Metallurgical and Materials Transactions A55,3327–3350;26June2024 publisher HTML
pages_equations_tables: Sections2–4; Eqs1–5,9–12; TableV discussion; Figs12–18 captions; Data Availability. Not every figure/table/appendix visually audited.
findings: AA5754,9mm initial hot band,100mm wide,50% one-pass reduction,410mm roll diameter,40mm/s,unlubricated. FEM deformation histories drive GIA,VPSC,DAMASK texture comparisons. Constant friction0.25 improves texture but overpredicts force44%; spatially variable friction improves joint agreement. DAMASK cost exceeds statistical models for these cases.
weaknesses_conflicts: High-shear laboratory case, not lubricated foil or multipass calibration. Force1121.5kN is labelled specific initially and roll force later; verify observation normalization. Empirical friction fitting is not independent validation. Data are in article or on request; raw repository not audited.

title: Mech421/6511 Lecture5: Rolling
version: M.Medraj, Concordia University; undated5-page PDF with20 lecture slides; no revision identifier
pages_equations_tables: PDFpp3–5, lecture slides11–20; flat rolling assumptions, slip, torque/power, worked example
findings: Teaching baseline defines draft, forward slip, constant-volume kinematics, approximate bite Δhmax=μ²R and per-roll torque≈FL/2. Two-roll power uses both torques and rotation frequency in consistent time units.
weaknesses_conflicts: Rigid-roll/infinite-sheet approximations. Listed generic friction values are teaching examples, not aluminium material cards. Single neutral-point and pressure-peak statements are not universal with hardening, sticking or elasticity. Geometric ln(hin/hout) is not automatically von Mises equivalent strain.
domain: Generic flat rolling; no calibrated alloy/temper
relevance: Unit/convention and limiting-case tests only; source cannot establish plant limits
access_notes: University-hosted PDF text read; relevant slides reviewed, no claim that every process illustration was visually inspected.

title: Rolling models: Adaptive setup models for cold rolling mills
findings: Separates scheduling,preset and adaptation. Circular reduction-mill model differs from noncircular-informed foil model. Loaded gap needs mill compliance/thermal expansion. Limits include reel/drive capability,temperature and quality; short pass-to-pass and slower coil adaptation are distinguished.
weaknesses_conflicts: OEM architecture account, not public equations/calibration dataset or project performance proof. Steel illustrations cannot become aluminium coefficients. Publication's approximate domain split is not a universal5% switch. Reported benefits lack reusable raw validation here.
domain: Industrial cold mills,steel and nonferrous including aluminium; mixed product regimes
relevance: State/equipment/settings contracts; offline calibration and later advisory architecture
access_notes: Official100-page magazine accessible; reviewed only six-page rolling article. Existing mapping43–47 truncates article: correct span43–48.
